details: The Federal Reserve's April inflation forecast has deteriorated, with the Cleveland Fed's Inflation Nowcasting tool projecting a trailing 12-month rate of 3.58% as of April 15, up from 3.28% at the month's start. This persistent inflation, largely driven by energy price shocks, reduces the likelihood of Fed interest rate cuts and could even prompt rate hikes, potentially impacting risk assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: US Inflation Outlook Worsens, Fed Rate Hikes Possible

details: Reports indicate that hardliners fired on ships attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, threatening peace negotiations. This renewed uncertainty is causing crude oil prices to rebound and is fueling inflation risks alongside fears of a global economic slowdown. Geopolitical developments in the Middle East are a primary focus for financial markets, with continued volatility expected in commodity markets, particularly energy.
title: Middle East Tensions Escalate, Strait of Hormuz Threatened

details: Central banks globally are closely monitoring the Middle East conflict's impact on energy prices and supply chains, which could reignite inflation. While the Federal Reserve is expected to maintain current rates, the European Central Bank and several Asian central banks may consider tightening monetary policy if inflationary pressures persist, shifting from potentially more dovish outlooks.
title: Global Central Banks Brace for Higher Inflation from Middle East Conflict
